subject.title: Bug: Telegram delivery queue recovery can replay old sendMessage replies and duplicate delivery-mirror transcript entries

question: Should OpenClaw quarantine or otherwise classify legacy Telegram outbound queue rows with missing `recoveryState` when their prior `sendMessage` outcome is ambiguous?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the product tradeoff between possible unsent-message loss and duplicate delivery requires maintainer intent before an automated fix should choose behavior.

options.title: Quarantine Ambiguous Legacy Rows
options.body: Move or mark legacy untracked Telegram rows as unsafe to blindly replay, preferring no duplicate user-visible Telegram send over possible loss of an unsent reply.

options.title: Reconcile Before Replay
options.body: Keep the rows pending unless an adapter or future ledger can prove the platform did not receive the original send.

options.title: Keep Replaying Legacy Rows
options.body: Accept the existing upgrade behavior and close only after documenting that legacy queued sends may replay.

recommendation.title: Quarantine Ambiguous Legacy Rows
recommendation.body: Move or mark legacy untracked Telegram rows as unsafe to blindly replay, preferring no duplicate user-visible Telegram send over possible loss of an unsent reply.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision fits the recent maintainer proof and landing ownership for the overlapping outbound recovery rewrite.
